label: Employed by Maryland University
description: Joseph Weber worked at Maryland University.

sources.quote: Joseph Weber, form Maryland University, was a pioneer in the experimental research of gravitational waves and neutrinos.

label: Studied under John Archibald Wheeler
description: Weber went to Princeton University under the supervision of John Archibald Wheeler.

sources.quote: Forced to change the research field, he went to Princeton University under the supervision of John Archibald Wheeler.

label: Designed bar detector
description: Weber decided to use a bar detector for gravitational waves.

sources.quote: In the early 1960s a clear picture of which astronomical events could emit gravitational waves around 1 kHz was not clear.

label: Claimed gravitational wave observation
description: Weber claimed to observe gravitational waves.

sources.quote: The first who claimed to observe gravitational waves in 1969 was Joseph Weber.

label: Braginsky showed quantum limit
description: Braginsky showed that resonant bar detectors were affected by the uncertainty principle.

sources.quote: In 1978 the Russian physicist Braginsky showed that resonant bar detectors were affected by the uncertainty principle.

label: Thorne proposed LIGO
description: LIGO was proposed by Kip Thorne.

label: LIGO observed gravitational waves
description: LIGO observed for the first time directly the ripples of spacetime.

sources.quote: 40 years later in 2016 LIGO observed for the first time directly the ripples of spacetime.

label: Proposed neutrino detection mechanism
description: Weber proposed a new mechanism to detect neutrinos with a very simple apparatus.

sources.quote: In 1984 Weber proposed a new mechanism to detect neutrinos with a very simple apparatus.

label: Published neutrino theory
description: Weber published theoretical work on neutrino coherent scattering.

sources.quote: The theoretical work of Weber of 1985 was criticized by two papers of 1986 and 1987.

label: Published neutrino experiment results
description: Weber published a detailed paper showing experimentally coherent scattering of neutrinos.

sources.quote: Weber in 1988 published a detailed paper where he showed experimentally how "coherent scattering of neutrinos can give measurable force due to coherent momentum transfer to crystal of cm of dimensions".

label: Team confirmed Weber's experiment
description: A team succeeded to confirm Weber's experiment on solar antineutrinos.

sources.quote: But in 2011 a team succeed to confirm Weber's experiment on solar antineutrinos.
